descriptions.text: $44.3 million drained in broad daylight. CoinDCX stayed silent for 17 hours - until ZachXBT forced their hand. The attacker funded from Tornado, routed through FixedFloat, and hit with precision. Hard to pull off something this coordinated without knowing where to look.

On July 19, on-chain investigator ZachXBT posted on his personal channel: “Looks like the India centralized exchange 'CoinDCX' was likely drained for ~$44.2M almost 17 hours ago and has yet to disclose the incident to the community.” Shortly afterward, the company confirmed the breach on X, describing it as a “sophisticated server breach” and stating that only corporate funds were affected.

CoinDCX lost about $44.2 million on July 19, 2025 after attackers compromised a single internal liquidity hot wallet via targeted social engineering. User funds were not affected, exchange operations continued, and the loss was absorbed by company reserves. No evidence of smart contract bugs or protocol exploitation. Credential theft through social engineering: malware installed on an engineer's laptop enabled unauthorized access to an internal hot wallet used for liquidity provisioning. The attacker initiated withdrawals using legitimate credentials, bypassing blockchain-level and user-facing security.

The Indian cryptocurrency exchange CoinDCX was hacked, with attackers stealing around $44 million. The company announced the breach the following day, attributing it to a "sophisticated server breach" and claiming that only company funds were impacted.
